theme: Strong, workable, and not cracking in a year
title: Not Just Less Water: Concrete Mix Design Under a Shrinkage Budget
strategies: reference baseline: default aggregate, no admixture, minimum cement, water exactly meeting that aggregate's demand (reproduces the checker's own construction -> ~0.1)

greedy textbook recipe: default aggregate, no admixture, water fixed at that aggregate's demand, cement pushed to the budget ceiling for maximum strength -- ignores that more cement and a thirsty aggregate both raise shrinkage-cracking risk, so it blows the risk budget outright on several instances

joint search over aggregate grading and admixture dosage: for each (blend, dosage) pair take the water demand it implies, then push cement to the largest value that still respects the shrinkage-cracking budget and the aggregate-volume floor -- decouples the workability requirement from raw water content instead of trading water against strength

a fuller solver could also exploit non-uniform coefficient tables per instance or interpolate between grid points for a slightly tighter optimum -- the grid search here already captures the qualitative decoupling insight
